title: Review scene: side-by-side profile comparison
what_the_feature_had_to_become: README B5 asks for a 旧/新 profile 对照. That wording predates D6, which deleted the legacy snapshot-diff route entirely, so there is no longer an 'old profile' to compare against. The two comparisons that are actually meaningful now are the live profile set against a candidate set, and one quality tier against another. Both are implemented.

bug_found_in_my_own_d5_work.what: BattleVfxReview's Run button never worked. compute_team_replay always returned empty.
bug_found_in_my_own_d5_work.why: the scene set only NetworkService.shared_seed and GameState.round_index. It never filled the boards or set team_active, so BattleSimulator had nothing to simulate. D5 only verified that the scene parsed, never that it ran a battle.
bug_found_in_my_own_d5_work.how_it_surfaced: the first A/B compare run printed 'Replay came back empty for seed 20260823 round 1'

shared_fixture_extracted.why: battle_presentation_baseline.gd and promo_capture.gd each carried their own copy of the lineup, with a comment asking the next person to keep them identical by hand. The review scene then shipped with no copy at all, which is the bug above.
shared_fixture_extracted.not_migrated: tools/promo_capture.gd still has its own copy; it is the user's promo tooling and out of scope here
shared_fixture_extracted.frozen_hashes_unchanged: the baseline was re-run after the extraction and all four frozen hashes matched exactly, proving the refactor changed no behaviour

compare_modes.候选 profile 目录: side A loads res://data/vfx/battle_cues/, side B loads a candidate directory. Verified with a candidate whose basic_melee windup was 120->240 ms and recovery 150->300 ms; the report showed cues_pending +1 at the shared frame, which is exactly the signal a longer windup should produce.
compare_modes.另一质量档: same profiles, two tiers. Verified HIGH vs LOW: draw calls 292->279, nodes 771->762.

how_it_stays_honest.same_moment: both sides are captured at the same replay frame, not 'when finished', or the two screenshots would show different moments of the battle
how_it_stays_honest.same_path: _start_run(tier, profile_dir) is what the manual Run button calls too, so the two sides cannot diverge in setup
how_it_stays_honest.override_cleared: the resolver override is cleared after every side and on _clear_screen(), so a stopped compare cannot leak into a normal battle
how_it_stays_honest.fps_caveat: side A always runs first and absorbs shader compilation and resource loading. Measured drift was about +26 fps for B on otherwise identical pairs, so the report and the status line both state that fps is not comparable and name what is: draw calls, nodes, tweens, pending cues, budget, adapter counts and the screenshots.

headless_entry_point: --review-compare with --seed / --round / --capture-frame / --tier and either --compare-tier or --compare-dir. Without it the comparison could only ever be run by a human clicking a button, which is also how the empty-replay bug survived D5.

battle_cue_profile_check.note: was 162; 7 new assertions cover the candidate directory loading all five profiles, the override defaulting to empty, and both tools sharing the fixture

known_limitations: The artist review itself still has not happened. B5 delivers the tool; the judgement is a human task.
promo_capture.gd still duplicates the lineup and can drift from the shared fixture.
The fps caveat is documented rather than engineered away; removing it would need a discarded warm-up run, which doubles the cost of every comparison.
